subsystems.name: Neural interface
subsystems.role: connects synthetic hardware to neurons for reading and writing signals.

subsystems.name: Biocompatible packaging
subsystems.role: protects the implant from the immune system and the body from the implant.

subsystems.name: On-board electronics
subsystems.role: processes neural signals and generates stimulation patterns.

subsystems.name: Power and data link
subsystems.role: supplies power and transmits data through the skull.

subsystems.name: Neurotransmitter delivery
subsystems.role: releases signalling molecules to communicate chemically with neurons.

subsystems.name: Surgical tooling
subsystems.role: places the module safely into the cortex.

buildSteps.title: Design the electrode array
buildSteps.detail: Choose geometry, materials and channel count to match the target brain region and expected signal types.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the probes
buildSteps.detail: Use photolithography on silicon or polymer to create micron-scale electrodes and insulated wires.

buildSteps.title: Package the electronics
buildSteps.detail: Assemble the integrated circuit and memory, then seal them in a biocompatible enclosure.

buildSteps.title: Coat for biocompatibility
buildSteps.detail: Apply anti-inflammatory and anti-fouling layers to reduce scarring and protein buildup.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the module
buildSteps.detail: Bond the electrode array to the electronics and the power/data link.

buildSteps.title: Test in vitro
buildSteps.detail: Verify signal quality, stimulation safety and material stability in saline and cell cultures.

buildSteps.title: Implant in animal models
buildSteps.detail: Use robotic insertion to place electrodes, then monitor for months to measure signal stability and immune response.

buildSteps.title: Human trials
buildSteps.detail: Eventually test in volunteers for safety, signal decoding and basic stimulation effects.

buildSteps.title: Scale up capability
buildSteps.detail: Increase channel count and add bidirectional stimulation aimed at memory and skill tasks.

prerequisites.why: current arrays lose signal within months to years because scar tissue forms around them.

prerequisites.tech: Wireless power and data transmission through tissue
prerequisites.why: inductive links work for low data rates, but high-channel-count systems need more bandwidth and power.

prerequisites.tech: Understanding of neural codes for memory and skill
prerequisites.why: neuroscience cannot yet write complex information into the brain in a reliable way.
the immune system attacks implanted devices, limiting their working life.
inserting thousands of electrodes without damaging tissue remains very difficult.

pathway.milestone: brain-computer interfaces that restore movement or communication in paralysed patients
pathway.unlocks: proof that neural signals can be read and used in real time.

pathway.milestone: wireless, high-channel-count implants with multi-year stability
pathway.unlocks: long-term use without wires and with far more data.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop stimulation for specific memory tasks
pathway.unlocks: limited enhancement of memory in lab animals and early human trials.

pathway.milestone: bidirectional interfaces that write skills or augment cognition
pathway.unlocks: speculative cognitive expansion, if the neural codes for learning are cracked.
